formal_statement: ∀ (gates : List PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) (out : Fin 7 → ℕ), (∀ g ∈ gates, (g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.and ∨ g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or ∨ g.op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not) ∧ g.inputs.length ≤ 2) → (∃ ι : Fin 1 → Fin gates.length, ∀ i : Fin gates.length, (gates.get i).op = PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.not → ∃ j : Fin 1, ι j = i) → (∀ (o : Fin 7) (x : Fin 7 → Bool), PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit.eval ⟨gates, out o⟩ (List.ofFn x) = decide (∃ v ∈ (![{0, 1, 3}, {1, 2, 4}, {2, 3, 5}, {3, 4, 6}, {0, 4, 5}, {1, 5, 6}, {0, 2, 6}] : Fin 7 → Finset (Fin 7)) o, x v = true)) → 14 ≤ gates.length
plain_statement: Take the seven lines {i, i+1, i+3} mod 7 of the plane of order 2 on 7 points. Every list of AND, OR and NOT gates on at most two wires, with at most one NOT gate, whose outputs give the OR of each line on every input has at least 14 gates, every gate counted.
title: One NOT gate saves nothing on the plane of order 2: fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT lists with at most one NOT gate for its seven line-ORs need at least 14 gates
